findings.evidence: PLPath.lean:641 defines map and :649–685 contains its basic laws; all six new proofs use only normalization, rays, and linear maps.
findings.fix: Move all six lemmas to PLPath.lean alongside the existing map API.
findings.issue: The six new mapping lemmas, from map_zero_linearMap through map_smul_id_injective, concern basic path normalization and mapping but require importing root-operator theory.

findings.evidence: Word.lean:47–52 defines lowerWord/raiseWord and :71–89 proves singleton and append identities; the new proofs use only cons and successor identities.
findings.fix: Move both lemmas to LSPath/Word.lean with the other elementary word identities, importing StringLength there as needed.
findings.issue: lowerWord_replicate and raiseWord_replicate are basic word/iteration identities placed behind the full similarity development.

findings.evidence: Crystal/Basic.lean:90 defines RootStep, :102–107 provides the constructors used in these proofs, and :10 already imports StringLength.
findings.fix: Move both to LSPath/Crystal/Basic.lean beside the single-step RootStep constructors.
findings.issue: reflTransGen_rootStep_of_raiseIter_eq_some and reflTransGen_rootStep_of_lowerIter_eq_some are general reachability lemmas that unnecessarily require similarity theory.

summary: Several foundational lemmas live in later theory files, forcing users to import unrelated root-operator or similarity infrastructure.
